blocks.content: The Panchayati Raj System represents rural local self-government in India. It aims to decentralize power and ensure people's participation in governance at the grassroots level. The system received constitutional status through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
1. Background of Panchayati Raj

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions in India.
It added Part IX and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution, transferring 29 functional matters to local rural bodies.
Establishes a uniform 3-tier Panchayati Raj structure: Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block), and Zila Parishad (district).
Gram Sabha forms the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system, comprising all registered voters residing in the village area.
Mandates 33% (one-third) reservation for women across all levels and a fixed 5-year term for every Panchayat.

blocks.content: • Village self-government existed in ancient India.
• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended democratic decentralization.
• The committee suggested a three-tier Panchayati Raj system.
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayats.
2. Constitutional Provisions (Part IX)
3. Three-Tier Structure
4. Gram Sabha
• Consists of all registered voters in the village.
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions in India.
• Acts as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system.
• Approves plans and budgets of the Gram Panchayat.
5. Gram Panchayat
• Executive body at village level.
• Members elected directly by villagers.
• The head is called Sarpanch or Pradhan.
6. Panchayat Samiti

rows: Direct implementation of village-level development schemes and welfare programs
Coordinates and consolidates plans of all Gram Panchayats in the block
District-level macro planning, supervision, and allocation of funds to blocks

blocks.content: • Works at block level.
• Coordinates activities of Gram Panchayats.
7. Zila Parishad
• Functions at district level.
• Supervises Panchayat Samitis.
8. Key Features of the System
• Three-tier structure of governance.
• Regular elections every five years.
• Reservation for SC, ST and women.
• State Election Commission for conducting elections.

items: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) originally recommended the 3-tier Panchayati Raj system; Rajasthan was the first state to adopt it in Nagaur district on October 2, 1959.
Article 243I provides for the constitution of a State Finance Commission every 5 years, while Article 243K establishes the State Election Commission for local body elections.
Reservation for SCs and STs is proportional to their population, while not less than one-third of total seats are reserved for women under Article 243D.

blocks.content: • State Finance Commission for financial review.
EXAM Important Facts
• 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) introduced Panchayati Raj.
• Gram Sabha is the basic unit of rural democracy.
• At least one-third seats reserved for women.
• Panchayat elections are held every 5 years.
